source.title: Llama Scope: Extracting Millions of Features from Llama-3.1-8B with Sparse Autoencoders
source.authors: Zheng-Fu He; Wentao Shu; Xuyang Ge; Lingjie Chen; Junxuan Wang; Yunhua Zhou; Frances Liu; Qi-Peng Guo; Xuan-Jing Huang; Zu-Xuan Wu; Yu-Gang Jiang; Xi-Peng Qiu

record.tranche_reason: The study compares SAE features at two dictionary widths on the same model and layer, using feature similarity and interpretations to examine changes with size.
record.gate_note: The feature-geometry case study and the wider-versus-narrower SAE comparison bear on feature relations across dictionary sizes. General reconstruction and sparsity evaluations do not measure the claimed splitting pattern and are not recorded as rows.
record.test_reason: Section 4.6 uses the Towards Monosemanticity approach (decoder cosine neighbours, UMAP, interpreted features) to compare 8x and 32x SAEs on Llama-3.1-8B L15R. It reports that a general 8x feature has more specific 32x neighbours, such as Brexit versus 'Historical movements'. This bears directly on V1 and V2 in an open large-model release. The evidence is a single hand-selected case study.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right. The authors say their geometry analysis confirms feature splitting enables discovery of new features. They base this on a coherent threats-to-humanity cluster with above-chance cosine similarity, and on a 32x Brexit feature whose nearest 8x feature is a general 'Historical movements' feature. They argue wider SAEs learn new features, not just compositions of existing ones. Separately, they find TopK and Vanilla SAEs share similar feature geometry.
record.recipe_differences: The study compares 8x and 32x SAEs in a Llama-3.1-8B layer using decoder cosine similarity, UMAP, and GPT-4o feature descriptions. Its geometry evidence is a selected-feature case study.
record.method_sensitivity: The geometry analysis is limited to the selected L15R feature and its nearest neighbors; comparisons include Vanilla and TopK SAEs.

fits_no_version.finding: TopK and Vanilla 8x SAE features at L15R are much more similar to each other than a random-SAE baseline (Figure 8).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: SAEs with different activation functions learn largely shared feature geometry.

fits_no_version.finding: Firing-frequency distributions of 32x SAEs shift toward lower frequency than 8x SAEs at fixed k=50 (Figure 4).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Wider SAEs with the same L0 have rarer-firing latents.

record.problems: The feature-geometry evidence is based on one selected feature at one layer, with feature interpretations generated by GPT-4o. It does not measure whether features partition the same input set, and the cosine-similarity reference is a random-projection baseline rather than an input-coverage test.
record.rows_left_out: No relevant feature-geometry results left out.

untested.parts: Whether the finer features together cover or partition the coarse feature's inputs. Any systematic measurement beyond one selected feature.
Other large models, layers or SAE releases. Only Llama-3.1-8B L15R is examined.
Whether larger-SAE latents decompose into combinations of smaller-SAE latents. Any quantitative test of novelty. Whether any dictionary size is complete.
Not tested. Local UMAP clusters are shown, but nestedness and a mirrored concept hierarchy are not assessed.

record.verdict_notes: This is mainly an SAE release paper. Reconstruction, sparsity, out-of-distribution and interpretability evaluations do not bear on splitting. The record's 'cannot_determine' states for r1 and r2 understate the result: they show the nearness part of V1. 'Partial' is more accurate, given the single selected feature and no coverage test.

versions.untested_parts: The study does not measure whether finer features partition the coarse feature's inputs or together cover roughly the same inputs.
The feature-geometry test is on one model, one layer, and one open SAE release; it does not establish the pattern across other large models or releases.
The study reports local feature clusters, but does not test nestedness or whether a hierarchy of concepts is mirrored in the model's representation.
Absorption and parent-child firing coverage are not assessed.

A selected example is used to show a novel wider-SAE feature, but the study does not test broadly whether larger latents decompose into combinations of smaller latents or whether any dictionary is complete.
The study does not test whether splitting is an artifact of the sparsity objective or compare Matryoshka SAEs.

rows.subject: Llama-3.1-8B
rows.operation_detail: Compared interpretations of decoder-neighbor features selected from SAEs of different widths.

conditions.value: one selected L15R-8x-TopK feature; six nearest features in each 8x SAE and 24 nearest features in the 32x TopK SAE

rows.measure: GPT-4o descriptions of top-activating samples and thematic coherence of the selected feature group
rows.value: The selected features were described as sharing a theme of harmful events, including wars, pandemics, natural disasters, and other harmful occurrences.
rows.note: This reports a coherent theme among selected neighboring features, but does not show that multiple finer features partition the inputs of a coarse feature.
rows.check: The 24 nearest 32x features carry finer themes (WWII, Vietnam War, COVID-19, Brexit) around a general 8x harmful-events feature. That is consistent with coarse-to-fine splitting near the parent direction, but coverage of the parent's inputs is not measured and the feature was selected by hand. Partial, not cannot_determine.

rows.subject: Llama-3.1-8B
rows.operation_detail: Measured pairwise cosine similarity among the selected decoder features and compared it with a random-projection reference.

conditions.value: 36 selected features across L15R-8x-Vanilla, L15R-8x-TopK, and L15R-32x-TopK

rows.measure: Farthest cosine similarity distance among the selected features
rows.baseline: Randomly mapped features: maximum pairwise cosine similarity 0.09 for 8x and 0.10 for 32x
rows.note: The text reports the selected features as more similar than the random reference. This geometric measurement does not establish input coverage or partitioning.
rows.check: The 0.28 minimum pairwise cosine exceeds the random maxima (0.09 for 8x, 0.10 for 32x) and the JL bounds (0.174, 0.186). This shows the finer features lie near one another and the selected direction, which is one part of V1. Input coverage is not tested. The baseline should also cite the JL epsilon values.

rows.subject: Llama-3.1-8B
rows.operation_detail: Compared a selected wider-SAE feature with its most similar feature in the narrower SAEs.
rows.measure: Feature interpretation and comparison with the nearest narrower-SAE feature
rows.baseline: The most similar feature in the smaller SAEs was a more general Historical Movements feature.
rows.value: The 32x TopK SAE had a distinct Brexit feature described as activating exclusively on that topic.
rows.locator: Section 4.6, “Wider SAEs Do Learn New Features”
rows.note: The authors present this selected example as evidence that the wider SAE learned a new feature rather than merely a frequent composition of existing features. It does not establish input partitioning or broad absence of canonical feature sets.
rows.check: For V1 this is one example of a general 8x feature ('Historical movements') having a more specific 32x counterpart (Brexit), observed in a single case. For V5 it fits the novel-latent part only by the authors' assertion: they claim it is not a linear combination of 8x features but report no reconstruction or decomposition measurement.

relation.reason: Section 4.6 reports its own size comparison (the 8x 'Historical Movements' vs 32x Brexit example) and a neighbour-cosine control. These bear on V1, V2 and V5.

tranche.reason: It follows the Bricken et al. (2023) approach: decoder cosine neighbours and UMAP across SAE sizes, with interpreted features (GPT-4o descriptions).

source_check.notes: 'Farthest cosine similarity distance 0.28' is compared directly with random maximum cosines (0.09/0.10), so it is the least-similar pair's cosine. Figure 7 has 36 labels, so the selected feature is one of the six 8x-TopK neighbours. Only Brexit is stated to be 32x. Vanilla SAEs are not in the release. Brexit counts as a split child for V1 and as a novel latent for V5.

statements.correction: Text: all 36 features (6 from 8x-Vanilla, 6 from 8x-TopK, 24 from 32x-TopK) relate to wars, pandemics, natural disasters and other harmful events. The Figure 7 labels include WWII (x3), Vietnam War and COVID-19 (x4), but their SAE can't be placed from the text. Brexit is stated to be a 32x-TopK feature whose nearest smaller-SAE feature is 'Historical Movements'.
statements.problem: The text does not say which SAE the WWII, Vietnam War and COVID-19 labels belong to. They are Figure 7 labels, and the extracted text has lost the figure's colours. Only Brexit is stated to be a 32x feature. The other numbers are correct.

statements.correction: Llama Scope release: 256 TopK SAEs (32 layers x 4 sites x 8x/32x). L15R-8x-Vanilla is a comparison SAE outside the release. 0.28 is the farthest-pair cosine among 36 features, against random maxima of 0.09 (8x) and 0.10 (32x). Only Brexit is stated to be a 32x feature.
statements.problem: It lists L15R-8x-Vanilla among the open Llama Scope SAEs. The release is 256 TopK SAEs; the Vanilla SAEs are comparison SAEs. The 32x attribution of the WWII, Vietnam War and COVID-19 labels can't be checked from the text; only Brexit is stated as 32x. The 0.28 'minimum pairwise cosine' reading is sound.

statements.correction: Text: the 36 features (6 Vanilla 8x, 6 TopK 8x, 24 TopK 32x) share a harmful-events theme. Brexit is a 32x-TopK feature whose nearest smaller-SAE feature is 'Historical Movements'. 0.28 is the farthest-pair cosine; random maxima are 0.09 (8x) and 0.10 (32x).
statements.problem: The text can't confirm that the WWII, Vietnam War and COVID-19 labels are on 32x features; only Brexit is stated as 32x. The 0.28 minimum-cosine reading is sound. The coverage gap is cited as V1.untested[2], which is about size sweeps; coverage is V1.untested[0].
